I give up. I did not change `/work/combi_imo_2011_p4.lean`, so it still contains the original `sorry`.

I checked the statement on small cases: n=1 gives 1 and n=2 gives 3, matching (2n-1)!!. So the theorem looks true, but I could not produce a complete Lean proof for general n.

The mathematical argument I worked out is this. Let G(m, j) count placements of m weights where only the first j steps are checked. The heaviest weight 2^(m-1) must sit on the left whenever it is checked, because it outweighs all lighter weights combined. Splitting on its placement time p gives G(m, j) = Σ_{p≤j} G(m-1, p-1) + 2(m-j)·G(m-1, j), with G(0, 0) = 1. Then G(n, n) = Σ_{q<n} G(n-1, q) reproduces (2n-1)!!.

The obstacle is formalization. Turning this into Lean means reindexing permutations of `Fin n` when the heaviest weight is removed, and building bijections between the filtered `Finset` of pairs `(σ, f)` and the recursive sequences. I could not carry that out reliably with the tools available here.
